# Syllabus {#sec-syllabus}

This is the syllabus for an approximately sixteen-week semester. For WPI
students, Canvas and the official academic calendar remain the authoritative
sources for policies and deadlines.

## Learning Outcomes {#sec-syllabus-learning-outcomes}

By the end of the course, students should be able to:

1. Explain where navigation sits in an autonomy stack: what it consumes from
   perception and sensors, and what guidance, planning, and control need from
   it (state, uncertainty, rate, latency, frames, and health).
2. Turn raw sensor data into measurement models, including a camera-based
   perception model, and justify the noise model with evidence.
3. Implement and compare probabilistic estimators built on Bayesian,
   Kalman-style (EKF, UKF, error-state), and Monte Carlo methods.
4. Build a landmark-based SLAM system and reason about data association,
   map growth, and consistency.
5. Integrate an inertial navigation system with GNSS on the curved Earth using
   an error-state Kalman filter.
6. Evaluate a navigation system using accuracy, uncertainty, consistency, and
   computational-cost evidence, and communicate the results in a technical
   report.

## Textbooks {#sec-syllabus-textbooks}

These notes are the primary text. They draw on:

- *Probabilistic Robotics* by Thrun, Burgard, and Fox [@ProbRob];
- *Robotics, Vision and Control* by Peter Corke [@corke2021robotics];
- *Principles of GNSS, Inertial, and Multisensor Integrated Navigation Systems*
  by Paul Groves [@groves]; and
- Roger Labbe's *Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python* [@labbe2020].

@sec-intro-textbooks-resources explains which of these to buy and which are
free through the WPI library.

## Course Requirements {#sec-syllabus-course-requirements}

The course is project centered, with three projects that build on one another
but remain individually assessable:

- **Project 1, visual-inertial navigation (@sec-project1).** Build a
  computer-vision perception model (AprilTag PnP) to see how navigation
  connects to the rest of the stack, derive its measurement model and noise,
  then implement a basic Cartesian-frame inertial navigator as an EKF, a UKF,
  and a particle filter, and compare them.
- **Project 2, Victoria Park FastSLAM (@sec-project2).** Extract tree landmarks
  from laser scans and estimate the vehicle path and map with FastSLAM.
- **Project 3, INS/GNSS integration (@sec-project3).** Mechanize a strapdown
  INS on the curved Earth and aid it with GNSS through an error-state Kalman
  filter.

Each submission includes source code and a technical report that explains
model choices, results, limitations, and the evidence supporting the
conclusions (see @sec-intro-project-guidance). The starter packages are in
Python, which is the supported language for examples and debugging help;
students may use another language when they can still meet the required
deliverables.

## Grading Policy {#sec-syllabus-grading-policy}

The course follows the standard A--F scale. Projects are weighted:

- Project 1: Visual-Inertial Navigation -- 50%
  - Dataset understanding and loading -- 10% of the project
  - Part A: mechanization and dead reckoning -- 20%
  - Part B: PnP observation model and covariance -- 20%
  - Part C: EKF, UKF, and particle filter -- 30%
  - Cross-method evaluation and technical communication -- 20%
- Project 2: Victoria Park FastSLAM -- 25%
- Project 3: INS/GNSS Integration -- 25%

Each project's rubric (in its handout) rates components as Excellent,
Acceptable, Marginal, or Unacceptable; an Acceptable rating corresponds roughly
to a B. Code that runs is necessary, but it is not by itself evidence that the
navigation model is correct. Higher ratings require clear justification of
state, measurement, covariance, and validation choices.

| Letter grade | Percentage |
|---|---:|
| A | 90--100 |
| B | 80--89 |
| C | 70--79 |
| D | 60--69 |
| F | Below 60 |

## Course Policies {#sec-syllabus-course-policies}

- **Deadlines.** All projects are due by the **end of week 16**. The weeks in
  the schedule below are a recommended pace, not hard deadlines; submitting
  early gets you feedback while there is still time to act on it. Extensions
  past the end of the semester are granted only in extreme circumstances and
  must be requested in writing beforehand (@sec-intro-grading).
- **Prerequisites:** see @sec-intro-recommended-prerequisites.
- **Reports:** expected structure and length are in @sec-intro-project-guidance.
- **AI tools and software libraries:** see @sec-intro-ai-policy-and-dependencies,
  including the rule for pre-built filtering libraries such as `filterpy`.
- **Course materials** are proprietary. Keep your solutions in a private
  repository and do not republish the notes, handouts, or starter code.
- **WPI policies** (academic integrity, accessibility accommodations,
  incompletes, and student support resources) are on Canvas.

## Course Schedule {#sec-syllabus-course-schedule}

The schedule sequences the book. The course is deliberately front-loaded: the
theory arrives early so the second half of the semester leaves room to
implement. The optional advanced chapters add no assessment requirements.

| Week | Topics | Recommended pace |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Course orientation; GNC; coordinate-frame and attitude conventions | |
| 2 | Linear algebra, probability, and scientific Python refresh | |
| 3 | Sensor taxonomy, motion models, IMU errors, and dead reckoning | Project 1 Part A |
| 4 | Measurement models, data association, and PnP vision | |
| 5 | Camera-to-robot observation models and covariance | Project 1 Part B |
| 6 | Bayes filtering and the Kalman-filter review | |
| 7 | EKF, error-state filtering, and consistency diagnostics | |
| 8 | UKF, information filters, and particle filters | Project 1 Part C |
| 9 | Filter comparison, project integration, and implementation review | Project 1 complete |
| 10 | Mapping, landmark SLAM, and data association | |
| 11 | FastSLAM, visual navigation, and loop closure | Project 2 |
| 12 | Global frames, GNSS measurements, and IMU error models | |
| 13 | Curved-Earth INS/GNSS integration and observability | Project 3 |
| 14 | Timing, health monitoring, validation, and production software | |
| 15 | Optional advanced topics: smoothing, GNSS receiver-to-fusion, and resilient navigation | |
| 16 | Integration, review, and project completion | **All projects due** |
